transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um, my mom actually wanted me to come in. I guess I've just been... well, I know I should be doing more, but mostly I just can't make myself do anything anymore. I've kind of just been sitting in my room. Sometimes I, um... I end up keeping the same clothes on for a while. I know that probably sounds really bad, I'm sorry, I don't mean to be lazy. 

I used to do things. I'd knit, and write in my journal, or go walking... but I just stopped. And when my mom comes in and asks what's wrong, I... I barely even have the energy to answer her. I really do want to be better, I promise. Is it... does that make sense, how I explained it?
Did this change start after a specific stressful event or life change?

Um... I've thought about that a lot, actually. Because I know it would make more sense if something bad happened, right? But... no. Not really. 

I just... I don't know. There wasn't a big fight or a trauma or anything like that. I feel really guilty about it, honestly, because I don't have a good excuse for being this way. I hope it's okay that I don't have a specific event to tell you about... I'm really trying my best to give you good answers, but I just don't think there was a trigger. Is that alright?
When you have to make decisions on your own, do you feel anxious or unable to do it without other people’s help?

Um... no, I don't think so. I hope it's okay that I say no to that. 

I mean, I don't really get anxious about making choices, and I don't feel like I absolutely need someone else to do it for me. It's more just... well, since I'm mostly just in my room, I don't really have a lot of big decisions to make right now. But when I do have to choose something, I can usually figure it out on my own. I just... I kind of just don't care very much about what happens either way, if that makes sense? 

I'm sorry if that's not a very helpful answer. I'm really trying to give you the right information. Am I answering your questions okay so far?
Have you been feeling this way most days for at least two years?

Um, yeah, I guess it has been that long. I hope that's not too frustrating to hear, that I've let it go on for so much time without getting help. 

I remember it started right around the time I tried to do a community-college program. That was... gosh, about two years and two months ago, I think? I really wanted to do well there, I promise I did, but that's when things just started getting harder. I didn't mean to let it drag on this long, I just kept hoping I'd snap out of it. Does that timeline help? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
During the past two years, has there been a period of at least two weeks when your mood was much worse than usual?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I hope it's okay to say that. 

I don't think I've had a time where things got suddenly worse for a couple of weeks. It's just been... well, pretty much the same this whole time. Just kind of flat, I guess. I haven't been crying all day or feeling super depressed or anything like that. I know that might make it easier to figure out what's wrong with me, and I'm sorry if I'm not giving you the symptoms you're looking for. 

I just want to make sure I'm being honest with you. Is it okay that it's just been kind of steady like this?
